nodes.name: NiFe LDH electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: A Ni-foam (NF) piece measuring 2 cm × 1 cm was sonicated in 10% v/v HCl for 10 min to remove its surface oxide layer. Subsequently, the residual acid was rinsed off using acetone, ethanol, and deionized water through sonication, each for 10 min. The NiFe LDH electrodes were fabricated using a standard three-electrode system comprising the NF (with a controlled geometric area of 1 cm × 1 cm), a platinum coil (EC-Frontier, CE-100), and a saturated calomel electrode (SCE, ALS, RE-2BP) as the working, counter, and reference electrodes, respectively. NiFe LDH formation occurred in an electrolyte containing Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (6 mM) and FeSO4·7H2O (6 mM) in DI water, with the deposition process involving a constant potential of -1.05 V vs SCE for 2000 s. After electrodeposition, the electrodes were washed and sonicated with DI water for 1 min to eliminate any residual electrolytes and particles from their surfaces.

nodes.name: BWO@NiFe LDH intercalation
nodes.procedure: BWO@NiFe LDH fabrication was conducted in an electrolyte solution of NaWO4·2H2O (6 mM) and boric acid (40 g/L) in DI water, heated and stirred at 50°C for 24 h to form BWO. After cooling to room temperature, boron tungstate intercalation into NiFe LDH was executed by applying a constant potential of -0.8 V vs SCE for various durations (20, 40, 300, 1200, and 1800 s). Following electrodeposition, all of the prepared electrodes were washed with DI water and dried.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDHs: Eg 455 cm⁻¹, A1g 540 cm⁻¹. BWO@NiFe LDHs and D-NiFe LDHs: Eg shifts to 450 cm⁻¹ (negative), A1g to 545 cm⁻¹ (positive), indicating lattice distortion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra of NiFe LDHs exhibited bands at 455 and 540 cm⁻¹ ... Both BWO@NiFe LDHs and D-NiFe LDHs displayed ... negative shift of the Eg lattice mode from 455 to 450 cm⁻¹ and a positive shift of the A1g lattice mode from 540 to 545 cm⁻¹

nodes.characterization_summary: D-NiFe LDHs show Ni binding energies shifted +0.3 eV and Fe +0.4 eV higher than NiFe LDHs, indicating higher valence states due to structural distortion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notably, the Ni-binding energies in D-NiFe LDHs exhibited a positive shift of approximately 0.3 eV and the Fe-binding energies ... showed a positive shift of approximately 0.4 eV compared to those in NiFe LDHs.

nodes.characterization_summary: D-NiFe LDHs stabilize β-NiOOH phase (Eg/A1g ratio ~1.2 constant) during OER, while NiFe LDHs transform to γ-NiOOH (ratio increases to ~2.1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In contrast, in D-NiFe LDH, the Eg/A1g ratio was relatively constant at around ~1.2, suggesting the generation of the β-NiOOH phase. ... this result indicates the formation of the γ-NiOOH phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals vertically aligned nanosheet arrays with highly porous architecture on Ni-foam substrate for NiFe LDHs before and after anion-exchange; morphology unchanged.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Low-magnification SEM images (Figure S1a-c) revealed vertically aligned nanosheet arrays with a highly porous architecture on a Ni-foam substrate. ... The anion-exchange process did not significantly alter the morphology of NiFe LDHs (Figure S1d-f).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and EDS mapping show homogeneous distribution of Ni, Fe, O, and W in BWO@NiFe LDHs; W absent in D-NiFe LDHs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) images and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping analysis revealed a homogeneous distribution of Ni, Fe, O, and W elements in BWO@NiFe LDHs, whereas the W element was absent in D-NiFe LDHs (Figure S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni L-edge and Fe L-edge EELS spectra show positive shifts of 0.5 eV and 0.4 eV respectively in D-NiFe LDHs compared to NiFe LDHs, indicating higher valence states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Similar results were observed in both Ni and Fe edge spectra using electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS), as shown in Figure S6. Notably, the L-edge EELS spectra of Ni and Fe exhibited positive shifts of 0.5 and 0.4 eV, respectively.
